investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing via Shared Upstream Dependency
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-15T01:00 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents. Because every check shares the same error message and no evidence was collected by any of them, the failure is localized to the swarm gateway layer, not to individual check logic or the eval runner itself.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB target reachable at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint used by POST /api/agents → /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api environment at the time of the eval run. This caused every remote-agent check to receive HTTP 502 before any agent provisioning could begin, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected. The failure is an eval-detected infrastructure availability issue scoped to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 is down, misconfigured, or has no healthy targets — the most strongly supported cause given the identical 502 across all three checks and the explicit 'swarm gateway unreachable' error text (failed-check.message)
Network routing or security-group change between production-api and the swarm ELB broke connectivity — consistent with a sudden, total failure affecting all remote-agent checks simultaneously
The swarm service behind the ELB crashed or was restarted and has not recovered, causing the ELB to return 502 with no healthy backends

A deployment or configuration change to the swarm service or its ELB listener rendered the /v1/agents route unavailable — no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so this remains a lower-confidence hypothesis

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful POST /api/agents response (2xx) from production-api at or near the time of the eval run would disprove gateway unavailability.
ELB access logs showing healthy 2xx responses to /v1/agents around 2026-09-15T00:59Z would indicate the problem is in the eval runner's network path or credentials rather than the gateway itself.
A passing run of remote-agent-create with non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all present) would confirm the gateway has recovered and the failure was transient.
If only one of the three sibling checks returned 502 while others passed, that would disprove the shared-dependency hypothesis and point to per-check logic instead.

Add historical run tracking for remote-agent-create so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be computed — the current packet shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, which prevents regression detection.

Consider a latency-only eval for the swarm gateway that fires a lightweight health-check request and asserts sub-second response, providing an early warning before the full provisioning path is exercised.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Feature: All Three Checks Failing with 502 Swarm Gateway Unreachable on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-15T01:00 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway backing POST /api/agents is unreachable. Because the failure occurs at the very first step of agent provisioning — before any evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) can be collected — every downstream contract assertion is also unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with error code "bad_gateway" and message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" on every attempt to POST /api/agents. Because agent creation is the prerequisite step for all three remote-agents checks, none of the checks could proceed past provisioning, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary: The AWS ELB target group backing the swarm gateway /v1/agents endpoint was unhealthy or had no registered healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the load balancer to return 502.

Tertiary: The swarm gateway service itself (the process behind the ELB) crashed or was restarting during the eval window, causing the ELB to return 502 while targets were temporarily unavailable.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-09-15T01:00 with an identical 502 bad-gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents provisioning step — before any agent identity, model, or runtime response can be captured — the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime received zero evidence fields.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check that calls POST /api/agents received HTTP 502 with error code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning". Because agent creation is the first step in the remote-agent-runtime probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), no agent was provisioned and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) could be collected, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a backend connectivity or availability problem localized to the swarm gateway / ELB endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing via Shared Upstream Dependency
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-15T01:00 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents. Because every check shares the same error message and no evidence was collected by any of them, the failure is localized to the swarm gateway layer, not to individual check logic or the eval runner itself.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB target reachable at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint used by POST /api/agents → /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api environment at the time of the eval run. This caused every remote-agent check to receive HTTP 502 before any agent provisioning could begin, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected. The failure is an eval-detected infrastructure availability issue scoped to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
